pr_title: Add support for json in adhoc -a
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Has ansible try and parse `-a` as JSON before falling back to the key=value if it isn't valid yaml/json.

Fixes: https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/78112

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME

issue_context.title: Allow ansible -a to parse from json
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Using the adhoc `ansible` cmd  parses the value of `-a` uses the key=value splitter. It would be good for it to support parsing from json allowing people to specify nested structures and have the command/win_command/shell/etc modules support extra options outside the hardcoded list at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/e8a77626a3b33832783433817108cbfbb84227ea/lib/ansible/parsing/splitter.py#L91.

review_comments: not sure we need json_only .. the yaml shorthand is more flexible and should allow people to use with a LOT less quote mangling

The reason why I went strict json is I don't want something like `-a '{{ variable }}'` to be read as YAML. Using strict json makes it a bit more stringent on what it will accept for the json data and have it fallback to the existing kv parser.
That already fails the YAML parser as a dictionary is not a hashable key
While it does seem to fail with pyyaml it is being parsed by yamllint so maybe in the future pyyaml might load it. I just kept it as json to be on the safe side.
yamllint is far from a good source of 'valid yaml' ...

Which in this case is valid yaml, it's just pyyaml that doesn't like it. I have no idea if that's going to change in the future. I prefer to be safe rather than sorry and someone else can implement yaml support in the future if they wish to pursue that path.
for it to be valid a dictionary  would need to be a valid key in a python dictionary
